source_facts.statement: The and family section is Syntax 'and.type d, a, b;' with .type including .b16 in PTX ISA 9.3 section 9.7.8.1.
Core semantics for and is 'd = a & b;'.
Notes state: operands must match in size, but not necessarily type; predicate registers are allowed.
Notes state introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0 and supported on all target architectures.
Examples in the and family examples block include .b32 forms; no explicit .b16 example is quoted.
General instruction-form context says instructions have operands d,a,b,c and optional guard; for result-producing instructions d is destination and a,b,c are sources.
General predication context says all instructions may have optional guard predicate '@{!}p' and unguarded instructions execute unconditionally.
Control-flow form @ states 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.'
Control-flow form @ semantics is 'If {!}p then instruction'.

derived_interpretations.statement: Bounded syntax for this run is and.b16 d, a, b; (three operands: one destination, two sources).
Operand role assignment: d is written; a and b are read, because semantics is d = a & b and result operand is positioned as first operand in 'd, a, b'.
Typing for the bounded form is .b16, so d,a,b are in a 16-bit value domain; operand sizes must match, while same-size type differences are allowed by family note.

Guard behavior is: no guard -> execute unconditionally; @p -> execute when p true; @!p -> execute when p false; guard false -> instruction does not execute and no state updates occur (do-nothing interpreted as no change).

No explicit memory/predicate/status side effects are described for and.b16 in the and section text; bounded behavior models destination register update only on execution, plus guard false no-op/no-state-change branch.
